title: Upgrade cadence, safety-horizon and compatibility matrix for runtime/API/SDK/Console
creator: Asha Khatri
description: We need a coordinated, machine-readable compatibility/support surface that maps LTS lanes and upgrade cadence across four inference surfaces: runtime, public API, language SDKs, and Redwood Console. Current patchwork decisions cause ambiguous developer expectations during rollouts and make emergency rollbacks risky. This ticket defines the 'safety-horizon' concept (explicit support windows + rollback guarantees), an automated matrix generator, and gating automation to block unsafe rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A stable CSV/JSON compatibility matrix exists that lists per-release support horizon, recommended upgrade cadence, and guaranteed rollback window for runtime, API, SDKs, console
Automated validation (api-compat-checker) runs as part of release CI and fails the pipeline if semantic breakage is detected for declared compatible pairs
Rollout gating rules implemented in canary-orchestrator: internal -> partners -> open with configurable cohort sizes and minimum observation windows
Documentation page published: 'Safety horizons and upgrade policy' with explicit dates/semantics for LTS, maintenance, and deprecation
A single runbook for emergency rollback that has been tabletop-tested and references exact metrics/dashboards to observe
tasks: Design safety-horizon taxonomy (LTS / Maintenance / Short-term) and map to support months per surface
Implement compatibility-matrix-generator service that queries build metadata and test matrices to produce JSON/CSV
Add api-compat-checker to SDK release workflow (java, python, node)
Extend runtime CI: run kv-cache-stress + kernel-shape-validator against previous minor releases to detect behavior regressions
Create rollout gating policy config in canary-orchestrator and integrate with console rollout UI
Author the public docs and internal playbook; include deprecation notice templates and customer communication cadence
Run tabletop rollback drill with SRE, Product, and Support; capture gaps and action items
notes: Safety-horizon proposal: runtime LTS = 12 months of active security/critical fixes + 6 months maintenance; API LTS = 9 months; SDKs = 6 months with weekly patch-streams; Console = 9 months.
Introduce 'compatibility fingerprint' — a short hash representing API surface, model signature, and KV cache layout. Use fingerprint equality as a fast-path compatibility check.
Gating thresholds: 95th latency regression > 10% OR error-rate delta > 0.5% blocks rollout; custom flags per customer cohort allowed.
Canary cadence recommendation: internal 48-72h, partners 5-7d, public ramp 7-14d with automated rollback if threshold exceeded during observation window.
We will defer long-term policy for hardware/quantization variants to a follow-up (runtime-compat-hardware-variations).
